narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Nothing material has changed in the weather pattern since the morning issuance, with conditions feeling slightly warmer and calmer, and drier than yesterday, which saw rain. Expect pleasant afternoon conditions giving way to a clear to partly cloudy evening, with focus turning to increasing rain probabilities heading into the weekend.

## Today's Forecast
- Daytime Temperatures: Highs reaching 29°C / 84°F, with overnight lows dropping to 18°C / 64°F.
- Rainfall: Unanimously dry across numerical models (0.0 mm / 0.0 in), though Kenya Met notes a slight localized potential for light evening showers in a few places.
- Wind: Afternoon southwesterly winds blowing at 16 km/h (9 kt) to 29 km/h (16 kt).
- UV Index: Reaching a peak of 9 (Very High) during midday hours.
- Air Quality: Modeled US AQI is Moderate (78–87, PM2.5 primary). Ground sensors at Kisumu Airport, Ochieng' Avenue, and Dunga Beach are all reporting readings over 3 hours old (stale), so current assessment relies on model data.

## Extended Outlook
Looking ahead to Saturday (Aug 22) through Monday (Aug 24), daytime highs will hold steady between 29°C–31°C / 84°F–88°F. Shower and thunderstorm activity is projected to ramp up on Sunday (Aug 23) and Monday (Aug 24), as ECMWF (100% Day+3 rain accuracy) and ICON show precipitation accumulation between 1.0–7.0 mm (0.04–0.28 in). For Days 4–7 (Aug 25–28), precipitation tapers off rapidly after Tuesday, returning the basin to warm, dry conditions with highs reaching 32°C–33°C / 90°F–91°F by Thursday and Friday. Note that extended guidance relies on Day+3 and Day+7 skill records where ECMWF demonstrates strong reliability at Day+3, while Day+7 remains provisional due to limited verification history.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe weather hazards are anticipated for the remainder of today. High UV radiation (peak index 9) warrants standard sun protection during peak daytime exposure. Increasing convective instability (CAPE) toward Sunday will elevate the risk for localized thunder and lightning over nearby highland slopes.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Surface winds over open waters will blow from the SW at 16 km/h (9 kt) to 22 km/h (12 kt) with peak gusts to 29 km/h (16 kt), turning southerly overnight. Lake waters will remain light to moderately choppy. Precipitation risks over the lake remain minimal through tonight, with organized convection suppressed until late Saturday night.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1007 hPa) and highest toward the south (1021 hPa) — a 14 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the northeast is deepening over the next three days, while pressure overhead is near-steady. Locally across Nyanza Basin, regional MSLP values range from 1015.3 hPa to 1017.4 hPa, showing a slight 24-hour falling trend of ~2.0 hPa. This pattern continues to drive moderate southwesterly afternoon lake breezes across the shore.

Individual ground air quality sensors currently report as follows: Kisumu Airport (A418534, AQI 69, PM2.5: 69.0 µg/m³), Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central (A418300, AQI 34, PM2.5: 34.0 µg/m³), and Dunga Beach (A418504, AQI 74, PM2.5: 74.0 µg/m³). Because all three ground stations carry stale readings (>3 hours old), air quality evaluation relies on CAMS atmospheric modeling (US AQI 78–87, Moderate).

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
For today's Day+0 call, weighting heavily favors Best Match (90% rolling 10-check rain accuracy) and ECMWF (+0.1°C high temperature error). Although Kenya Met indicates isolated light showers, all numerical models unanimously project 0.0 mm, aligning with Best Match's superior rain calling track record.

Regarding long-run review findings over 10 verified checks (2026-08-11 to 2026-08-20): At Day+0, Best Match is the strongest rain caller while GFS is the weakest. GFS, ECMWF, ICON, UKMO, and Best Match all systematically under-forecast peak surface wind at Day+0, while ICON over-forecasts overnight lows (-2.3°C error) and UKMO under-forecasts overnight lows (+1.5°C error). At Day+3, ECMWF holds a 100% rain accuracy rate across 7 checks, though data sufficiency notes indicate this sample size is directional and not yet sufficient to formally rank models. At Day+7, only 3 verified checks exist, which is insufficient to rank models or establish long-term skill profiles.
